passage: Exams began in three weeks, so Noor had a single Sunday and two evenings to spare. On the kitchen table he wrote his skills: fixing phones, drawing, teaching basic maths. His sister Vandana, home from college, read over his shoulder. “Now ask which ones are allowed for someone your age, and safe,” she said. Noor crossed out the phone stall in the market: it wanted full days and ran till nine at night. Drawing wedding-card sketches at home on Sundays stayed. Maths lessons for the neighbour's child after school, in daylight, in their own building, stayed too. “Show it to Mum before you say yes to anybody,” Vandana added. Noor sighed at the crossed-out line; he had liked the phones best. Then he copied the two remaining lines onto a clean page.

qa.a: Fixing phones, drawing and teaching basic maths.

qa.q: How did Noor feel about crossing out the phone stall?
qa.a: Disappointed but sensible: he liked the phones best, yet accepted that full days and late hours did not suit school or his age.

qa.q: What could Noor do to test an option before committing, and why?
qa.a: He could start with one small trial, such as tutoring the neighbour's child for a month, because it shows whether the work fits around exams before he takes on more.

qa.q: How might Vandana see his plan?
qa.a: Vandana, who asked him to check what suits his age and to show Mum, would likely feel reassured that he thought about safety and school before taking on paid work.

grounding: A sixteen-year-old lists skills and checks which suit his age, are safe and fit around school.

passage:
Imran was sixteen and wanted to earn his own money this summer, like his older cousins in the Mumbra flats. But when Vandana, his neighbour, asked, "Doing what?", he had no answer.

So that night he made two lists in his notebook. First: what he could do. Fix cracked phone screens, he'd done six for friends. Draw portraits. Teach basic maths to younger kids. Speak decent English.

Second, beside each one: was it allowed and safe at sixteen? Would it fit around school and coaching?

Phone repair needed a shop, and the shop owner had asked for full days. Crossed out. Portraits at the Sunday market: maybe, with his mother nearby. Tuition for two Class 5 kids in the building, three evenings a week: legal, safe, near home, and done by seven.

He circled the tuition. Next morning he told Vandana. She said her little brother needed exactly that.

qa.q: How many phone screens had Imran fixed for friends?
How might Imran have felt when Vandana asked "Doing what?"
qa.a: He probably felt caught out and a bit embarrassed, wanting to earn but with no plan yet.

qa.q: What else should Imran check before starting the tuition?
qa.a: He should talk with his parents about the timings and the families, so an adult knows the plan and agrees it is safe.

qa.q: How might Vandana see Imran's tuition idea?
qa.a: Vandana seems pleased, since her little brother needs exactly that help, close to home.

grounding: Shows a sixteen-year-old listing his skills, then checking which work is legal and safe for his age and fits around school, and choosing tuition.

passage:
"You want a job? Doing what?" Raghav asked, spinning a football on his finger in the lane behind their houses.

"That's the problem," Jagdish said. "I'm sixteen. What can I actually do?"

"Okay, list it."

Jagdish counted on his fingers. "I can fix bicycles. I did Papa's and half the colony's. I can edit videos, sort of. I'm good at English grammar. And I can draw logos."

"Great. Now which ones are allowed?"

"The cycle shop wanted a boy full-time. That's school hours, so no. Video editing for that guy online who wouldn't give his name? No way. Grammar tuition for kids in our building, two evenings a week? That's fine. Logos for Mausi's boutique? Also fine, from home."

Raghav stopped spinning the ball. "So, tuition and logos."

"And nothing past seven. Mummy will check anyway," Jagdish said, grinning.

qa.q: How many evenings a week would the grammar tuition be?
How did Jagdish seem to feel before listing his skills?
qa.a: He seemed unsure and a bit stuck, wanting a job but not knowing what he could actually do.

qa.q: What else should Jagdish confirm before starting?
qa.a: He should agree on the timings and pay with his parents and the families, so the work stays safe and fits school.

qa.q: How does the plan look to Raghav?
qa.a: Raghav seems convinced, stopping the ball to sum it up, as the list narrows to two sensible options.

grounding: Shows a sixteen-year-old listing his skills, then ruling out unsafe or school-clashing options and choosing legal, safe work near home.
